headline: Tropical Equatorial Peatland Demarcation and Land Use Analysis in Borneo's Pontianak Delta Using Geospatial Approach
name: Tropical Equatorial Peatland Demarcation and Land Use Analysis in Borneo's Pontianak Delta Using Geospatial Approach
description: This investigation addresses critical deficiencies in Indonesian Indicative Map of Delay in Granting New Permits (IMDGNP) peatland boundary estimations through systematic verification of peat soil distributions in Pontianak City, West Kalimantan Province. Preliminary IMDGNP cartographic products at 1:250,000 scale identified four administrative districts containing peatland formations totaling 23.8649 km² , exhibiting documented accuracy limitations requiring comprehensive field validation. The research methodology integrated systematic field reconnaissance encompassing 614 observation points at 250-meter intervals, laboratory classification testing of 68 undisturbed soil specimens following ASTM D4427 (organic content > 75% threshold) and ASTM D2974 (ash content < 25% threshold) standardized procedures, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) spatial analysis for refined boundary demarcation at 1:50,000 scale. Results demonstrate that peat soil formations are confined to only two districts —Southeast Pontianak (5.798 km² , 35.95% of district area) and North Pontianak (17.320 km² , 42.14% of district area) —contrary to preliminary four -district estimations. Contrary to the preliminary four -district IMDGNP estimate of 23.8649 km² , verified peatland formations total 23.118 km² and are confined to only two districts. Within North Pontianak District specifically, the verified extent (17.320 km² ) exceeds the preliminary district-level IMDGNP estimate (12.7683 km² ) by 35.76%, while Pontianak City and East Pontianak districts contain organic soils rather than peat formations. The updated demarcation mapping incorporates peat layer depth information within a comprehensive geospatial database suitable for infrastructure planning , foundation design optimization, and building conserv ation, thereby supporting evidence -based urban development and environmental management aligned with tropical peatland ecosystem governance principles.

hasPart.name: 1. INTRODUCTION
hasPart.description: This section introduces the study's background, highlighting the critical discrepancies in Indonesian Indicative Map of Delay in Granting New Permits (IMDGNP) peatland boundary estimations in Pontianak City. It establishes the motivation for utilizing geospatial approaches and field investigations to accurately demarcate tropical equatorial peatlands.

hasPart.name: 2. RESEARCH METHODS
hasPart.description: This section details the methodological framework employed for field data collection, laboratory testing, and geographic information system analysis. It outlines the processes used to determine sampling locations, conduct soil testing, and process spatial data.

hasPart.name: 2.1 Study area
hasPart.description: This subsection describes the geographical characteristics of the study area within the Pontianak Delta in Borneo. It details the regional topography, climate, and administrative zones relevant to the peatland distribution.

hasPart.name: 2.2 Field investigation and data collection
hasPart.description: This subsection explains the procedures and protocols followed during on-site field investigations. It highlights the collection of ground-truth data to support subsequent geospatial assessments and soil classifications.

hasPart.name: 2.3 Sampling strategy
hasPart.description: This subsection outlines the overarching strategy utilized to design an efficient and representative sampling network across the target peatland zones.

hasPart.name: 2.3.1 Sampling location determination
hasPart.description: This subsection describes the criteria and techniques applied to pinpoint exact geographic sampling coordinates within the study area. It ensures optimal coverage of varied land use types and preliminary peat formations.

hasPart.name: 2.3.2 Field sampling procedures
hasPart.description: This subsection details the physical extraction protocols used to retrieve soil samples from the field. It covers depth measurements and preservation steps necessary for accurate laboratory analysis.

hasPart.name: 2.4 Organic content and ash content testing
hasPart.description: This subsection explains the laboratory testing methods employed to quantify organic and ash content in the retrieved soil samples. These parameters are crucial for verifying true peat soil composition versus mineral soils.

hasPart.name: 2.5 Geographic Information System analysis
hasPart.description: This subsection introduces the GIS framework utilized to integrate spatial data components and process digital maps. It forms the computational foundation for spatial modeling and boundary refinement.

hasPart.name: 2.5.1 Spatial data components
hasPart.description: This subsection lists and categorizes the various spatial datasets, remote sensing imagery, and administrative vector layers incorporated into the geographic database.

hasPart.name: 2.5.2 Geographic Information System development and processing
hasPart.description: This subsection describes the software workflows, overlay operations, and interpolation techniques used to process spatial layers within the GIS environment.

hasPart.name: 2.6 Research flowchart
hasPart.description: This subsection provides a comprehensive visual and descriptive flowchart summarizing the sequential stages of the research methodology from data collection to final mapping.

hasPart.name: 3. RESULTS AND ANALYSIS
hasPart.description: This section presents the primary findings derived from field investigations, laboratory soil tests, and GIS-based spatial evaluations. It thoroughly discusses land use classifications and refined peatland boundaries.

hasPart.name: 3.1 Field investigation results
hasPart.description: This subsection details the empirical findings obtained directly from the field surveys, contrasting initial maps with ground realities.

hasPart.name: 3.1.1 Preliminary peatland distribution from Indicative Map of Delay in Granting New Permits map
hasPart.description: This subsection analyzes the baseline peatland distribution data extracted directly from the IMDGNP maps prior to ground verification.

hasPart.name: 3.1.2 Land use classification results
hasPart.description: This subsection outlines the classification categories of land cover and current use identified across the verified study zones.

hasPart.name: 3.2.1 Organic content testing results
hasPart.description: This subsection presents laboratory findings regarding the percentage of organic matter present in collected soil samples, confirming peat characteristics.

hasPart.name: 3.2.2 Ash content testing results
hasPart.description: This subsection evaluates the ash content test outcomes, providing insight into the mineral versus organic makeup of the tested soil strata.

hasPart.name: 3.3 Data analysis and evaluation
hasPart.description: This subsection integrates field soil data with spatial overlays to rigorously evaluate ecological conditions and land use compatibility in the study area.

hasPart.name: 3.3.1 Land use assessment in verified peatland areas
hasPart.description: This subsection evaluates how existing anthropogenic activities and land uses overlap with the newly verified peatland extents.

hasPart.name: 3.3.2 Peatland demarcation refinement and boundary
hasPart.description: This subsection discusses the adjustments and corrections made to historical peatland boundaries based on empirical field evidence.

hasPart.name: 3.3.3 Peat soil layer depth classification
hasPart.description: This subsection categorizes the verified peat deposits according to their measured depth strata, providing a critical metric for ecological management.

hasPart.name: 3.4 Geospatial mapping and GIS assessment
hasPart.description: This subsection focuses on the geospatial analysis outcomes, utilizing spatial modeling to contrast baseline datasets with verified outputs.

hasPart.name: 3.4.1 Comparative analysis: IMDGNP vs verified boundaries
hasPart.description: This subsection provides a rigorous comparative evaluation highlighting spatial discrepancies, mapping errors, and accuracy gaps between the official IMDGNP data and ground-truthed boundaries.

hasPart.name: 3.4.2 Final demarcation mapping products
hasPart.description: This subsection presents the final cartographic outputs and high-resolution mapping products generated to assist future land-use planning and environmental protection in Pontianak.

hasPart.name: 4. CONCLUSION
hasPart.description: This section synthesizes the primary findings of the investigation, emphasizing the vital need for high-resolution geospatial verification in regional peatland governance. It provides final recommendations for policymakers to update official mapping standards.
